headline: Sensex Ends 22 Points Lower; Nifty Gains As Metals Rally
why: IT stocks drag benchmark indices ahead of the US Fed interest rate decision.
Higher US Treasury yields weigh on global investor sentiment.
Rally in metal and FMCG sectors provides strong support to the Nifty.
AAII survey shows global investor sentiment plunging to a 16-month low.
whatHappening: Sensex slipped 22 points while Nifty gained 53 to 75 points in a volatile session.
Smallcap index jumped nearly 1.8% outperforming the benchmark indices.
SBI report highlights FCNR(B) could generate ₹5 trillion notional profit for banks over 5 years.
Air India CEO considers folding its budget unit into the group to streamline costs.

summary:
Indian benchmark indices ended on a mixed note as the Sensex dropped 22 points while Nifty gained ground, supported by strong performance in metal and FMCG sectors.
Global market sentiment remained subdued due to rising US Treasury yields, rate hike concerns, and investor confidence dropping to a 16-month low.
Domestically, broad market participation was robust with smallcaps jumping nearly 1.8% and banks eyeing strong long-term FCNR(B) deposit profits.
